strengths: The results of this paper are truly captivating.
It manages to generate images of impressive quality with just one or two steps.
The quality showcased in the figures is highly satisfying.
In addition, the paper provides a detailed account of various experiments and the corresponding performance metrics, which adds greatly to its value.
The writing style of the paper is extremely clear.
It provides a very good introduction to the framework of rectified flows for a reader without deep knowledge of the topic, and overall the manuscript is quite self-contained.
The conducted experiments provide a sufficient support for the motivation of the method. I find the evaluation thorough enough.

The results achieved in the paper are definitely interesting for the broad community of ML researchers and practitioners due to the achieved combination of required computational resources for the model training and inference and its performance.
The paper is well-written, and the experiments conducted are both sufficient and convincing.
The InstaFlow achieves amazing performance (1-step inference with reasonable quality in approximately 0.09 seconds).
The contribution is great. Making the conditional diffusions work with one or very few steps will greatly boost the development of diffusion community.
The comparison experiments are carefully and fairly set up, and I appreciate that.
weaknesses: The paper appears to be a straightforward application of RECTIFIED FLOW with no clear novelty in the algorithms or methods presented.
The model that claims to operate in 1 step actually resembles a configuration of two UNets linked together, and thus feels closer to a 2-step process.
When the refined model from SDXL is not applied, the results show a noticeable degradation in high-frequency details.
This submission is more an extension of the previous work [1] rather than an independent work; the novelty is limited and the work is too incremental although helpful for practitioners.
While the idea of Stacked U-Net is interesting, the paper lacks ablation studies to justify the design choice versus increasing depth or channels of a conventional U-Net.
The paper provides results only for latent models and lacks comparison with cascaded models such as DeepFloyd IF [2], limiting the evaluation scope.

While this model demonstrates impressive performance, it involves a trade-off between inference speed and generation quality, with artifacts (e.g., distorted faces, blurred textures, fragmented object boundaries) inherited from the 2-Rectified Flow and potentially amplified by the one-step distillation process, indicating robustness concerns.
Concern about storage overhead due to needing a large (noise, image) pair dataset for the distillation or reflow process.
Question regarding the intrinsic difference between the distillation and reflow processes and need for clarification.
Question about the noise scheduler mismatch (normal diffusion scheduler vs. linear scheduler) and the time embedding used in the SD UNet.
Question why the model predicts "x1-x0" instead of "x1-xt" and considerations behind this choice.
